steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since {{pt_you}} got the braces off with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still holding straight, a little shifting starting, or moved back quite a bit. Which one is closest?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Holding Straight
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. After all that time in braces, a straight smile that stays straight is the whole goal. It means the retainer is doing its job.

(Let them enjoy it. Then ask permission for the questions.)

steps.title: A Little Shifting
steps.content:
That's common, {{contact_first_name}}. Teeth want to drift back toward where they started, especially once the retainer routine slips, and {{pt_no_fault}}. It's the reason we check in. When shifting is caught early, it's usually much easier to correct. What do you think made it start, the retainers wearing out or not getting worn as much?

(Let them answer. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Moved Back Quite a Bit
steps.content:
That's common, {{contact_first_name}}, and please don't feel bad. Teeth want to drift back toward where they started once the retainer routine slips, and {{pt_no_fault}}. It's the reason we check in. Your notes say {{pt_you}} left with a smile to be proud of. What do you think made it come back, the retainers wearing out or not getting worn as much?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, teeth move so slowly that nobody catches it happening. Can I ask a few quick questions about how the smile is holding up?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to the shifting in a moment. First, can I ask a few quick questions so {{pt_your_file}} is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, the shifting. Is it mostly the front teeth, or crowding coming back?

How about the retainers, still going in at night, and do they still fit?

Any changes in {{pt_your}} bite, like teeth hitting differently or chewing more on one side?

How about flossing, any tight spots where the floss catches or shreds?

Any jaw soreness, clicking, or headaches in the morning?

How does {{pt_your}} smile feel in photos these days, still showing it off?

Finally, anything the dentist has flagged since we last saw {{pt_them}}?

(Recap what you wrote down, including the shifting, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between the shifting and anything else you mentioned, which one would you most like to take care of?

(If the shifting is the only thing on the list, that's the answer. Tap the button and continue.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, any shifting or crowding at all since the braces came off, even something small?

How about the retainers, still going in at night, or has the routine slipped a little?

Any changes in {{pt_your}} bite, like teeth hitting differently or chewing more on one side?

How about flossing, any tight spots where the floss catches or shreds?

Any jaw soreness, clicking, or headaches in the morning?

How does {{pt_your}} smile feel in photos these days, still showing it off?

Finally, anything the dentist has flagged since we last saw {{pt_them}}?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing came up, that's still a good call. Use the second button.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been on {{pt_your}} mind, like a few weeks, or longer than that?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "Got it.")

Is it something that comes up now and then, or every time {{pt_your}} smile is in a photo?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "I see." or "I understand.")

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, smiling around people, or {{pt_your}} confidence?

(Let them answer. Reflect only what they said about the smile or confidence; with a parent, refer to their child, not the parent. If no impact, you can say "Got it, thank you.")

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on {{pt_your}} mind a while, and it comes up most times there's a photo. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, smiling around people, or {{pt_your}} confidence. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd love to see {{pt_them}} showing off that smile again without a second thought. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. A quick check shows us where the teeth stand compared to the day the braces came off. If it's minor, a refreshed retainer or a short touch-up is often all it takes. If everything is holding better than you think, we'll tell you that too. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}} for that quick check, so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. Does that sound reasonable?

(Say "does that sound reasonable", not "does that sound good". Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad everything is in good shape.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Do not argue with it.)

(Tap the button below that is closest to their reason.)

steps.title: If They Say: “I was happy with the results”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}, and that's the best reason there is. When the smile looks right, coming back stops feeling urgent. One thing worth knowing. Even when everything feels like it's holding, retainers age. They stretch, warp, and wear thin, and teeth take advantage of that. A quick check makes sure everything is holding where it should.

Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}} so we can check those retainers and keep that smile where it belongs. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Budget
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad you told me. A retainer check is a short visit, and it costs a fraction of what the treatment did. And you're not committing to anything. It's one visit so we can make sure the retainers are still doing their job.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}} for that quick check. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and a retainer check slides down the list. It happens to everyone. The visit is quick, and we can find a time that works around your schedule.

Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}} at a time that's easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back if the teeth shift”
steps.content:
That's a fair way to think about it, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd share is that teeth move slowly. You usually don't notice until they've been drifting for a while. Caught early, it's often a refreshed retainer or a short refinement. Caught late, it's a lot more than that.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}} so we catch anything early. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: They Moved or Tried Another Provider
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're still in the area, we'd love to see {{pt_them}} again. The records and the whole history are in {{pt_your_file}}, so we can pick up right where {{pt_you}} left off.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}}. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Parent Mode
steps.content: (Parent mode is on. Every screen from here uses parent or guardian wording automatically.)

steps.title: Objection: “Braces again?”
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's the first thing everyone asks, and the answer is usually not.

Can I ask, does it feel like a tooth or two moved, or the whole bite?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices or promise treatment lengths on the call. The check decides that.)

Teeth drift a little at a time, and small drift is a small fix. Caught early, it's often a refreshed retainer or a short touch-up, not a second round of braces. Wait a year and the same drift becomes a bigger job. The check shows exactly how far {{pt_your}} teeth have moved, so you'd know what it takes before deciding anything.

{{provider_name}} can do that check in one short visit.

Would it help to know it's a small fix before you assume it's braces?

steps.title: Objection: “How long would fixing it take?”
steps.content:
That's the right question, {{contact_first_name}}, and I won't guess at it.

Can I ask, is it the months you're worried about, or the number of appointments?

(Let them answer. Do not promise treatment lengths on the call.)

It depends on how far things have moved, and that's why the check comes first. Small drift caught early is usually a short, simple fix. The same drift left another year gets longer, not shorter. After the check, {{provider_name}} can give you a real number for {{pt_your}} teeth instead of a range.

Would it help to have that number before you decide?

steps.title: Objection: The retainer routine slipped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, please don't be. Nobody here is keeping score.

Can I ask, did the retainer break or get lost, or did wearing it just slip off the routine?

(Let them answer. Stay warm.)

Either way, teeth drift the moment the retainer routine slips. That's how teeth behave, and {{pt_no_fault}}. The only thing embarrassment does is keep people away until it's a bigger job than it needs to be.

{{provider_name}} would rather see {{pt_them}} now than a year from now. We'd take a look at {{pt_your}} teeth and figure out the shortest path back.

Would it feel better to just get that first step done?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like clear aligners, another office, or just a new retainer?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all make sense, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is how far {{pt_your}} teeth have moved and what that needs. {{provider_name}} already has {{pt_your_file}}, the scans and the original plan, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the cost of the check itself, or the worry about what a fix would cost?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

This first check is one appointment, not a treatment. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide on it. And since you've been here before, we're not starting from scratch, and starting from scratch is the expensive part.

The other side of it is what the shifting is already costing {{pt_them}}, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first check, or the worry about a long treatment again?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one check. {{provider_name}} looks at {{pt_your}} teeth and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that’s a refreshed retainer. Sometimes it’s a short touch-up, and you’ll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is signing {{pt_you}} up for anything on the phone.

We'll fit that first check around your schedule, not the other way around.

Could you find a short window for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that {{pt_your}} teeth have shifted. After the check, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{pt_your}} teeth have shifted. It's been that way for a while, and it hasn't sorted itself out on its own. The check is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you what's realistic for {{pt_your}} teeth specifically. That takes {{provider_name}} looking at {{pt_them}}, and that's one short check.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
